Britain’s competition regulator on Wednesday opened an investigation into Unilever’s
$65B food business merger with U.S. spice maker McCormick
, examining whether the deal could reduce competition in the UK.
Phase 1 decision deadline is set for Nov. 11, 2026.

If the ​deal goes through, it would create ⁠one of the world's largest flavorings and food products companies, combining household ​brands such as Knorr, Hellmann's, French's, and Frank's RedHot as food manufacturers seek scale to ​offset rising costs and changing consumer ​demand.
The deal, announced in March, will leave Unilever

and ⁠its shareholders owning 65% of the fully diluted equity of the combined company, including a 9.9% stake to ​be held ​directly ⁠by Unilever, while McCormick shareholders will own the remaining 35%.

title: UK regulator probes Unilever food business’ $65B McCormick merger
